data.value: Windows Server / Active Directory – Group Policy

data.name: TrustWindowsActiveDirectoryDescription
data.value: In Group Policy Management, open Computer Configuration › Policies › Windows Settings › Security Settings › Public Key Policies › Trusted Root Certification Authorities. Import the downloaded root CA as a .cer file and link the policy to the target computers.

data.name: TrustOpnSenseDescription
data.value: Open System › Trust › Authorities › +, select Import an existing Certificate Authority, paste the root CA as PEM, and save. If services need a complete chain, configure intermediate CA handling under System › Trust › Settings.

data.name: TrustVmwareDescription
data.value: For vCenter, import the root CA as a trusted root CA in certificate management. In current vSphere versions, use Menu › Administration › Certificate Management › Trusted Root Certificates › Add. For an individual ESXi host, browser trust is configured on the accessing client; for TLS connections to other services, use the relevant host or vCenter trust management.

data.name: SshHostTrustDescription
data.value: Add the host CA to the clients' known_hosts file so signed host keys are accepted without a fingerprint prompt.

data.name: SshUserTrustDescription

data.name: SshConfigureUserCaTrust
data.value: Copy the user CA to the server and extend sshd_config
